tasks.description: The addendum (recommendation 2) keeps assignment internal but lets the user influence it through the lead prompt: prefer a named provider for a task, keep code changes on this machine, give a task to a connected testing session, or take a task themselves. SO-L-A as signed has a deterministic fallback and one coordinator; it has no assignment preference input. This contract adds the preference as an event the planner records and the coordinator reads: an eligibility input, visible and editable, that never skips a gate, a permission or a valid transition. The conversion of the user's words into a structured preference is the lead session's work through the project tools (SO-05-A); memev makes no model call. When the preferred resource is unavailable or unsuitable the system explains and proposes a safe alternative instead of switching silently.

criteria.statement: memev work prefer (and the same instruction through the project tools) records an assignment preference, distinct from the lead preference of SO-L-A AC02, at project, workstream or task level, as an event carrying the user's words, the affected work ids, the resolved preference (provider, tool, machine or human owner) and a feasibility verdict; the preference is shown by memev work status (SO-08-B AC06) and is changed only by a later preference event, never by editing task state

title: SO-A-01 Lead agent: assignment preferences and overrides in ordinary language, recorded as inputs to the plan, never as direct mutations of execution state
request: Build layer of the Scope One programme, adapted from the unsigned fold of 30 Oct 2026 (fold id SO-A-01) and validated against memev main at d1c65ef. Contracts marked with a dagger are signed in the owner's vault and are not visible in this repository; they are cited by id only. Implements the design record SO-1.03 (Lead assignment: a default suitability analysis and an in-language user preference) (contracts/scope-one/specs). The decision record cites this contract by id and keeps only the gaps this one does not cover. Builds on signed vault contracts: SO-02-A†, SO-03-A†, SO-05-A†, SO-08-A†, SO-C-A†, SO-L-A†. Memev contracts that land first: SO-1.01. Source in the fold: #222 recommendation 2 (optional user-directed assignment and control; state-machine enforcement; progressive control). Settled decisions this contract follows (owner decision 31 Oct 2026, docs/scope-one/DECISIONS.md): topology is local-first and the cloud is only a relay and a backup; every supported provider stands on equal footing and no work or tier depends on one; crdt-merge is reached only through the provider boundary of src/engine/merge.mjs (docs/EXTENSION-POINTS.md) and this contract adds no merge engine to the core; tiers follow docs/PRICING.md (Free core, Personal for up to 3 computers with no per-computer add-on, higher tiers by contacting us) with no Personal trial; the git backup keeps running every few minutes (sync.interval_min). Memory authority: ADR 7 (memory and project-state authority) is proposed in PR #325 and is not decided here; this contract cites it and the local-first decision, and keeps one store under the vault with no second database. Provenance: adapted from the unsigned fold of 30 Oct 2026. Changes: (1) converted from the vault task format to the memev spec format (named tests run as red-green checks on the own test file of the contract; inline regular expression flags became the flags key; hygiene and decision verifiers became commands or doc checks). (2) removed fold-only fields and the owner-decision marker field, reworded the stop rule that named a patent, and made the text pass the leak scan. (3) Prerequisite added: SO-1.01 (delivered by #326), because preferences are read by the coordinator that now reaches the state machine; the fold named only vault prerequisites. (4) The fold tool name project_preference_propose becomes memev_project_preference_propose, following the memev_task_* and memev_project_* names registered in src/server/mcp.mjs. (5) Added a provider-neutrality test (owner decision 31 Oct 2026): with two equally eligible resources of different providers and no preference, the choice does not depend on the provider.
